  Reported: "Could not read live status (stale): stale / Could not read the   
  fleet                                                                       
  (stale): stale" — every call from one part failing, permanently, with no    
  path                                                                        
  back except a human rebuilding and redeploying that part.                   
                                                                              
  ## What happens                                                             
                                                                              
   net/client.ts  compares the response's  x-exposure-shape  against the      
   shapeHash  baked into the generated client, and returns  { kind: 'stale' } 
  when                                                                        
  they differ. That check is right and it caught a real drift.                
                                                                              
  But there is nothing after the detection. Every subsequent call fails the   
  same                                                                        
  way, forever. The part is dead until somebody notices, regenerates, rebuilds
  and                                                                         
  redeploys it.                                                               
                                                                              
   GET /api/_describe  now exists and serves the current shapes. A stale      
  client is                                                                   
  exactly the client that should fetch it.                                    
                                                                              
  ## And the endpoint currently refuses to help                               
                                                                              
   _describe  answers 409 EXPOSURE_MISMATCH when the request carries an       
   x-exposure-shape  that differs from the server's. For a discovery endpoint 
  that                                                                        
  is backwards: the descriptor is what a stale client fetches in order to stop
  being stale, so refusing it is a recovery deadlock. It is unreachable today 
  only                                                                        
  because the client never sends that header — which is a bug waiting rather  
  than a                                                                      
  bug avoided.                                                                
                                                                              
  ## What to build                                                            
                                                                              
  A client that discovers it is stale should be able to obtain the current    
  shapes                                                                      
  and say what actually changed, instead of returning the word "stale" five   
  times.                                                                      
                                                                              
  Decide and justify: whether recovery is automatic (refetch and retry once)  
  or                                                                          
  reported (surface which calls moved, so the failure names itself). I lean   
  reported — a client whose types were generated against the old shapes cannot
  safely use new ones just because it fetched them, and silently retrying     
  against a                                                                   
  changed API is how a wrong answer looks like a working one. But a  stale    
  error                                                                       
  that carries the difference is worth far more than one carrying the word    
  "stale".                                                                    
                                                                              
   exposureDifference  already exists in  mesh-                               
  serve/src/api/schema/descriptor.ts                                          
  and computes exactly that.                                                  
                                                                              
  ## The underlying drift, for context — not yours to fix                     
                                                                              
   describeExposure  and the runtime route table build  CallShape             
  differently: the                                                            
  descriptor includes  errors ,  routes.ts:128  does not. Two computations of

  hash over two differently-built inputs. That is a separate issue against    
  mesh-serve.
